node.body:
This adds linked drill-downs for reports, building on the query builder changes in #2926.

It adds helpers to recipe columns that build a predicate, like `status.Equals("open")`, which goes in a report's `Filter` on its own, or combined with others via `recipe.All(...)`. Each predicate produces both the `sqlb` clause for the report's query and a filter on its drill-down table.

Most reports follow this pattern, where the `Filter` is just the SQL form of the drill-down filters we already define. For any that don't, `FilterSQL` takes a raw `sqlb` clause, which goes into the query but not into the drill-down filters.

A source can set a default drill-down that its reports inherit, and a report can opt out with `recipe.NoDrillDown` when the filters can't express its predicate (an `OR`, for example). A ratio report's drill-down lists the rows in its numerator.

This PR also adds a few columns that seemed useful and let more reports use linked drill-downs.

commit.messageHeadline: ledger: Share a report's filter predicates with its drill-down's filters
voip recipe: Add drill-downs filtered by each report's predicates
ledger changelog: Note a same-day change gets its own heading

nodes.bodyHTML:
I think this is ready now. I've added default drill-downs to the source builders and folded in your suggestions about the predicate API. Adding the default has linked a bunch more drill-downs, but I think they all make sense.

I also added a note to CLAUDE.md about changelog headings, because it keeps getting them wrong and appending to an existing one, which reposts the whole entry in chat

if/when FilterSQL is used, does anything warn you / make you confirm that you've set up the drill-down correctly?

I'm torn on variables vs column names for the predicates, it does feel a bit more awkward to declare the columns as variables up front
not sure if it'd be better, but you could now make predicates their own type, with public ToClause and ToFilter methods

nodes.bodyHTML: could this hand a clause to the query builder instead of implementing the interface?

what's your thinking with this?

it implements the interface so it can be walked and nested inside other sqlb clauses, but I hadn't really considered doing it another way

when I wrote this I hadn't realised it sits inside the existing sqlb field - with a strict mode it might be reasonable to have a plain Filter field, and then an optional FilterSQL or similar if you need to drop down a level?

Done! I think it works pretty well, and it removes a bunch of the checks we needed for sqlb.Or etc.

I made it accept either a single predicate or a set of them wrapped in recipe.All() so single-predicate reports read better
